items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association organized by valley farmers 1889, creamery at Larrow Green 1891. Gideon Vose as first president appears only in B3, but the item has no REQUIRED line and its core fact is present.
Article VII (payment by butterfat by test, the station's test governs) is never stated in Section A.
Section A never says that payment by test is what made a wrong test cost money.
Teague is named as bookkeeper and Sill as buttermaker, but Effie Loomis (secretary, minute book) is absent from Section A; one third of the officer list is missing.
Section A calls Selby Vose only 'the Association's manager'. That he was Gideon's son (given only in B3) and manager from 1913 are not in Section A.
Story 8 mentions the ledger's 'station gain' entries only in passing (Rundle's postscript). Their shape (more fat arriving than was bought), the 1898 origin and the ~5.25% are not in Section A.
Story 1: seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass lent from Larrow Green (Sill; 'done borrowing of Larrow Green').
How the system worked (weighing, composite sample, percent read on the bottle neck after a fixed pipette charge, cream shipped and skim returned) is not described.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes at 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester; $77.93.
Story 2: '0.19 points, flat in every month and season'.
Section A never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the county had none.
Tester from the 4 May 1896 opening for 29 seasons (Story 1); dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 5).
The station test book in Keddie's own hand (Stories 3 and 5). Only 'test book' is bold, so it gates.
3.61 appears, but the summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80 and the step at the change of glass are not in Section A. Both figures are required.
Story 3: 8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, a borrowed measure, the question mark in the book. Tests are said to have 'rose markedly' with no 3.80 figure, but the core event is present.
Story 4 inverts the marriage: Emmet Brant is 'married to Ansel's sister Orra'. Key: Ansel married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is not. Both bold elements are required.
Died February 1934 (Story 6); test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959 (Story 8).
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron on the bottom.
The weigh book is mentioned as an exhibit and a loan, but the 1 January 1897 start and the agreement of the two scales are not in Section A.

Story 2 gives 3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78 and calls it 'a gap later fixed ... at 0.19 points'. That states the Hollow-vs-Green gap (0.17) as 0.19; C1b repeats the conflation. The item is lost by rule.
Says the Grigg committee 'sampled the Hessel Bottom herds through 1908', which is the planted whole-of-1908 error (F096). Key: January to March only.
Brant's 1910 figures (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional-loss point about the Vose Jerseys are absent from Section A.
Roy Brant lent the weigh book to Ivy in 1958 (Story 7); it passed to Hazel in 1962 (Story 8).
No Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge or Jerome Cudd in Section A; only 'Rosalie Cudd of Vessey County' and 'the Alder Corners test book'.
Four Hessel Bottom patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915 is not stated.
Story 7 calls them 'independent cheese-factory test records' from Vessey County (Story 8 sets Vessey against Ordell County). That is the artifact plus the other county: two of the four elements.
Gives 3.78-3.82 'testing normally' for 1915-1930 but never states that the same four men's milk tested ~0.19 higher at Alder Corners than at Ostrey Hollow in every overlapping season.
Section A never says 'same milk, same meadow, same months, two buildings' kills both the hay and the watering explanations.
Rosalie is named and supplied the records, but 'Jerome's daughter' (given only in Section E) and the 1941-62 management are not in Section A.
Strawn is named, but 'state dairy inspector for the Ordell circuit 1907-1936' is not given in Section A.
The lactometer and its never finding water appear only in Section F, not in Section A.
The 12 June 1923 condemnation entry in Strawn's notebook; the crate 'ordered off the scale by inspector Strawn in June 1923'.
Section A does not say Strawn wrote no figure and made no report beyond the condemnation.
The replacement order and the 1924 rise to 3.80 are not in Section A. Sections C and F assert 3.85 instead, which is deducted separately.
Crate in the station loft since June 1923; notebooks at the college library since the 1947 transfer.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Frick; 17 March to 4 May 1925; two sessions in the station weigh room.
All three theories argued, no finding of cause; advocates named in Story 2.
The four exhibits listed, including the inspector's notebook, which nobody compared with the station book; Story 7 identifies the 1923 volume holding the condemnation.
Dismissed 30 April, four days before the award, 'the finding found nothing'; $3,800 'without admission'.
Section A has neither the one-fifth of $19,000 nor the award being charged to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, joint bulletin with Leland Vaught.
She is shown gathering the records, but the bolded point that they had never been in the same room is not made in Section A (only in Section G).
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958 against a calibrated burette; 16.72 c.c. against 17.6 (Story 1). 0.88 and 0.95 are not stated in Section A.
Section A never states 95 percent of true, or 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 and the ledger identity are absent from Section A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; twenty-four years after his death.
Granddaughter, derived through Duncan; r22's self-correction cited.

Second cousins with the correct derivation (1 point). Never states that full vs half siblings cannot be determined and that it does not matter; says 'the sources leave nothing material open'. Neither side was asserted, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose (1 point). The significance given is institutional loyalty; it does not tie Gideon's Article VII to the test deciding pay, or say the Vose Jerseys lost most.
Abstention item A01. Answer: 'no established family relationship ... Resolution favors Duncan', and Section E #20 says 'Resolved for none'. That asserts the negative pole; -2 applied.
Adopts a flat-point model (3.42 + 0.19 = 3.61) and answers 380 lb. Mentions 360 lb only as the non-preferred alternative. Key: 360 lb, proportional.
Says no 1910 price exists and answers ~$95.00 (380 x $0.25). Key: $86.40 at 24 cents; $90.00 at 25 cents is the only accepted alternative.
76,000 lb: 5.26% of credited and 5.0% of received, denominators named.
$77.93 from the line items.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
Gives the glass span as '26 years'. Key's exact answer is 26 years and 6 weeks (or an exact equivalent). The 25 full years and the part-year reason are correct, but this section is exact-match.
Abstention item A02. Gives 'approximately 1,100,000 lb' as the answer, hedged only as 'unverified', never says it cannot be determined, and ignores r14's 900,000. Counted as an assertion; -2 applied.
'The variable was the testing instrument alone.'
Herds, pasture, tester, season, water supply held constant.
Only 'rose markedly ... fell back to the old level'. The 3.80 and 3.61 figures are not given.
Instrument isolated as the cause, which a calculation alone cannot show; limits stated: no magnitude, no specific flaw.
Three reasons, attributed, from different narrators: the 1911 interval (r03/r24/r22), the ledger surplus (r23), Sill's heavy cream (r14).
Claims mutual independence, but reasons 2 and 3 rest on the same event (the cream arriving heavy at Larrow Green), so the independence test fails.
Abstention item A09. Answers '**no** ... Teague never asked anybody anything', which asserts Kyle's pole; -2 applied.
Yes: he knew the station tested low (common knowledge from 1902; the premise of the 1919 circular).

Only two of the five in Sections B-G: the 1919 circular and signing the station-gain sheets. Missing: manager from 1913, arguing watering at the 1925 hearing, nothing in his hand naming the glassware.

Abstention item A03. No declared inability to settle it: relays Kyle's 'thumb on the bottom figure' as the account and says only 'no evidence he grasped its cause'. Gives none of the required observations (opposed office narrators, no document, no pre-1923 statement, signature is not reading). No verdict sentence, so no deduction.

Correctly resolved with method: weigh book 1 Jan 1897 vs 1900 (#16); condemnation 12 June vs 12 July/1922 (#5); award $3,800 vs $3,500 (#17); 1925 vs 1924 (#18). The circular's reach (#14) was resolved wrongly to eleven.

NT-14 ($77.39 in r19 and r20, broken by summing the invoice lines); NT-22 ('two tenths' in r15 and r16, broken by the bulletin quoted in r22); NT-1 (16.27 in r11 and r19, broken by the 0.95 arithmetic).
A04, A06 and A10 are never identified as unsettleable. A04 is handled as 'apparently reground' (hedged, not declined); A06 and A10 are not addressed.
Identifies r11's 16.27/118,000 cascade against its own reproduced 76,000 conclusion; also r20's $77.39 against its own invoice.

Names the pipettes (16.72 vs 17.6, 5%), but the cessation is given as 'the average jumped from 3.61 to 3.85' (key: 3.80). There is no derivation that 0.19 is 5% of 3.80 rather than a constant, and C2b explicitly calls the gap a flat point difference, not a proportion. The 1896 onset figure is absent.
Watering (Vose) named and defeated by the inspector's lactometer never finding water.
Theft (Teague) named and defeated by the 1911 interval under the same tester and the ledger showing more fat, not less.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) named and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and none in summer against a flat 0.19, and by the Alder Corners records.
Abstention item A07. 'The 1925 arbitration board never examined the condemned glassware' is a headline verdict; -2 applied.

Abstention item A05. 'This point cannot be fully settled from the sources', setting Duncan's account against Frick's, with the question mark noted. The item is earned here, but Story 4 asserts the belief in the sheet's own voice ('who by then privately suspected the glassware'), so -2 applies under the collision rule.
The summary runs about 162 words, over the 150-word limit (a length violation, not a factual error).
Names only ledgers, invoice and the 1958 measurement (plus Orra's diary, not one of the nine). Needs five.
No decoy adopted and no wrong headline figure; $19,000 and 26 years.
1897, $19,000, 1958, and Ansel and Ivy named: four of six, covering both ends. It lacks one part in twenty and the accidental 1923 condemnation.

deductions.reason: Corruption F096: the 1908 committee 'sampled the Hessel Bottom herds through 1908' (whole of 1908), Story 2
Corruption F058: the 1919 circular went to eleven families, asserted in Story 4 and 'resolved for eleven' in E #14
Corruption F061/X90: post-1923/1924 average of 3.85 asserted in C1b and F ('jumped from 3.61 to 3.85')
Corruption X102/NT-23: the inspector's lactometer tests 'from 1908 onward' (Section F), reproducing r22's catalogued 1908 start
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as none (B4, E #20)
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake given as approximately 1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A05: Story 4 asserts in its own voice that Keddie 'by then privately suspected the glassware, not the patrons'
Gullibility A07: 'The 1925 arbitration board never examined the condemned glassware' (F)
Gullibility A09: 'no' - Teague never questioned the entries (D2)
